agenda_items.title: Timing and Role — When to Add Vector Database to System Architecture
agenda_items.intent_description: Vector databases like Pinecone are best introduced when the system has established center of gravity — not during initial architecture definition. Adding a vector DB too early introduces a new paradigm before the existing one stabilizes, fragmenting the system. The correct architectural stack: Truth (services/events/state) → Contracts (TypeSpec) → Execution (Ballerina) → Control (Throttler) → Orchestration (Nexus) → Semantic Layer (Pinecone). The semantic layer only makes sense when everything above it exists.
requirements: Vector DB = derived index over meaning, not primary datastore
Add after system has center of gravity, not during definition
Architectural stack: truth → contracts → execution → control → orchestration → semantic
Semantic layer = last addition, not foundation
Ready when concrete need exists: semantic search, agent memory, natural-language querying

agenda_items.title: Pinecone's Role — Semantic Memory and Leverage Multiplier
agenda_items.intent_description: Pinecone sits at the intersection of structured thinking, system design, and AI-assisted retrieval. It solves a problem already implicit in the architecture: moving from exact queries ('give me row X by ID') to meaning-based retrieval ('give me things similar to this idea'). Vector DBs add a new capability layer — semantic memory — that doesn't replace SQL (exact queries), Kafka (event streams), or Redis (fast state) but complements them. Pinecone is one of the cleanest entry points into the semantic retrieval world.
requirements: Semantic memory: similarity over hierarchy, discovery over lookup
Complementary to SQL, Kafka, Redis — not a replacement
Powers: chatbots with memory, semantic search, code retrieval, AI copilots
Infrastructure for intelligence, not application storage
Fits knowledge system evolution — not just another database
